text:
anya: Quick sync: I prototyped a tiered-coalescer that separates "hot" short-deadline traffic from "cold" warmup-heavy traffic. Wanted feedback on queueing tradeoffs.

anya: Observations so far: mixing warmup-candidates with short-deadline requests causes sporadic head-of-line latency spikes.

dave: Are you running separate queues per class or a single queue with priority tags?

anya: Separate logical queues inside the coalescer. Scheduler picks from high-priority queue if any deadline-almost. Cold queue gets a separate budget to emit warmup hints.

rico: How do you enforce the "separate budget"? token bucket? credits?

anya: Credits per-node and per-tenant. Cold queue consumes warmup_credits; when exhausted it stops emitting prefetch hints and falls back to strict-queue mode for that tenant.

karen: That sounds promising. Need to ensure cold queue doesn't starve the hot queue during bursts.

anya: Exactly. We do a weighted round-robin with dynamic weights: hot gets 70% by default but weight can be reduced if hot latency is healthy.

rico: What's the cost model for warmup hints? We need a way to estimate memory and fetch cost so we don't overcommit.

anya: WarmupHint includes: estimated_rows, worst_case_bytes, expected_keys_touched. We keep a cheap LUT to convert to memory cost. Hints are advisory and TTL'd.

karen: Any plan for preempting large batches that form due to cold queue draining its credits? Head-of-line risk again.

anya: Yes — at execution time we cap per-tenant token_emission. If batch tokens > tenant_cap we split into micro-batches and mark the first micro-batch as high-priority to avoid blocking. We also increment a `split_pressure` counter.

richter: (typo) rico: How about tracing and determinism on splits?

anya: We attach stable batch_id and split_index. Replays use the same split boundaries. All operations are idempotent at the operator boundary.

(dave): Rollout suggestion: feature-flag the warmup hint emission and the split logic separately. Start with splits enabled, hints disabled.

anya: Agreed. Splits are safer to land. Hints can be opt-in per-pool.

infra-bot: alert 2026-01-30T23:11Z - transient GPU memory pressure detected on node pool beta during prefetch storm.

karen: That alert is what prompted this. We need a per-node warmup_memory_budget that the coalescer consults before emitting hints.

anya: Implemented a simple check: if node_warmup_bytes + proposed_hint_bytes > node_budget => reject hint, emit backpressure event.

rico: Backpressure semantics? Do clients get a signal or do we just stop issuing hints?

anya: Both. The coalescer emits internal backpressure (soft/hard) and also returns a client-facing suggestion {mode: "immediate" | "coalesce", suggested_prefetch: n}. Clients may fallback to immediate ack. TTL short.

dave: Telemetry we should capture: per-queue wait_ms, hint_accept_rate, warmup_bytes_allocated, split_count_by_tenant, backpressure_events.

karen: Add a rollback trigger: if p95 latency increases > 15% or warmup_bytes > 60% node_budget for 3m, auto-disable hints for the pool.

tj: Client-side: SDK should honor suggested_prefetch and switch modes quickly. I'll add a tiny circuit-breaker in the SDK.

anya: Plan: land split-only patch to staging pool gamma with 2% traffic, collect split_count and latencies for 24h. Then enable hints behind opt-in flag in pool delta.

dave: I'll instrument Prom rules and create dashboards. Also add a loadtest trace that mimics heavy KV-warmup patterns.

rico: I'll help with the node-budget math and a small simulator to tune default budgets.

karen: I'll draft the rollout doc + runbook and the alerting thresholds.

anya: Great volunteers. Scheduling a 30m sync tomorrow to walk through the PR and dashboards.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: pushed split-only branch to staging-gamma at 6177779100.

anya: Thanks all — will post PR link and short checklist in the issue. :rocket:

karen: LGTM.

tj: 44d
